stem: During kidney transplant candidate evaluation, which finding is listed as a major contraindication to transplantation?

options.text: Untreated current infection
Early referral when glomerular filtration rate is below 30 mL/min
Completion of a smoking cessation program
Well-controlled hypertension on current therapy

explanation.rationale_correct: Major contraindications to kidney transplantation include untreated current infection. Active infection must be addressed before proceeding with transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Early referral when approaching advanced chronic kidney disease is encouraged, not contraindicated.
rationale_incorrect.C: Completion of smoking cessation is a condition that may be required for approval, not a contraindication.
rationale_incorrect.D: Controlled comorbidities are evaluated individually; untreated infection is explicitly listed as a major contraindication.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 8, Evaluation of Adult Kidney Transplant Candidates — Table 8.1 (Major Contraindications) → Untreated current infection

references.locator: Ch. 8 → Table 8.1 Major Contraindications to Kidney Transplantation → “Untreated current infection”; PDF p. 227 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: Which cardiac test is included in the standard pre-transplant evaluation workup for adult liver transplant candidates?

options.text: Echocardiogram and/or cardiac stress testing
Routine coronary bypass surgery before listing
Cardiac catheterization for every candidate regardless of symptoms
No cardiac assessment unless the candidate has chest pain

explanation.rationale_correct: Liver candidate evaluation includes echocardiogram and/or cardiac stress testing (dynamic or nuclear) as part of cardiac assessment before transplant.

rationale_incorrect.B: Surgical coronary revascularization is not a universal listing requirement for all liver candidates.
rationale_incorrect.C: Catheterization may be used when indicated, but the standard workup lists echocardiogram and/or stress testing—not mandatory catheterization for all.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cardiac assessment is part of the structured pre-transplant evaluation, not deferred until symptomatic chest pain occurs.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 12, Liver Transplantation — pretransplant evaluation → §2. Other tests → d.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 12 → pretransplant evaluation → §2. Other tests → d. Echocardiogram (ECHO) and/or cardiac stress testing; PDF p. 646 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: A candidate is approved for the waiting list with conditions pending further requirements. Which condition aligns with a common program selection practice described in transplant nursing education materials?

options.text: Completion of a smoking, drug, and/or alcohol cessation program
Immediate transplantation before psychosocial evaluation
Permanent exclusion from any future transplant consideration
Mandatory identification of a living donor before any listing

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidates may be approved with conditions such as completion of smoking, drug, and/or alcohol cessation programs before final listing decisions are implemented.

rationale_incorrect.B: Psychosocial evaluation is part of interdisciplinary selection; transplantation does not proceed before required evaluations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Conditional approval is not the same as permanent exclusion from transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Living donor availability is not a universal condition for deceased-donor waitlist activation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education — §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.ii (approved with conditions)
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Completion of smoking, drug and/or alcohol cessation program

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).

stem: When a transplant program declines a deceased-donor kidney offer presented through DonorNet, what documentation must be provided to UNOS?

options.text: A reason or refusal code
No documentation when the surgeon verbally declines
Documentation only for accepted offers
A refusal code only when the candidate is permanently inactive

explanation.rationale_correct: Whenever a deceased-donor kidney offer is declined, a reason or refusal code must be provided to UNOS even though the accepting physician makes the final decision.

rationale_incorrect.B: Verbal decline without coded documentation does not meet UNOS reporting requirements.
rationale_incorrect.C: Declined offers require refusal documentation, not only accepted offers.
rationale_incorrect.D: Refusal codes are required for declined offers regardless of candidate inactive status.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Allocation of Deceased Donor Kidneys — DonorNet offer paragraph (before Table 5.1)
primary_anchor.quote_hint: whenever an offer is declined, a reason or refusal code must be provided

references.locator: Ch. 5 → DonorNet paragraph (“whenever an offer is declined, a reason or ‘refusal code’ must be provided to UNOS”); PDF p. 113 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

references.citation: OPTN/UNOS — Policy 18.3: Recording and Reporting the Outcomes of Organ Offers (HRSA).

stem: A kidney candidate is listed on the UNOS waiting list but marked inactive. Which reason BEST explains inactive status according to standard waitlist management references?

options.text: Evaluation is incomplete or new issues have developed that may temporarily contraindicate transplantation
The candidate has completed transplantation and is awaiting discharge
Inactive status permanently removes all accumulated waiting time
Inactive listing means the candidate is ineligible for any future activation

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidates may be listed inactive when evaluation is incomplete or new issues arise that may be a contraindication to transplantation, often on a presumed temporary basis.

rationale_incorrect.B: Inactive status applies to candidates awaiting transplant, not to recipients who have already been transplanted.
rationale_incorrect.C: UNOS policy changes have allowed waiting time accrual for some inactive periods; inactive status does not automatically erase all waiting time.
rationale_incorrect.D: Inactive listing is often temporary while issues are resolved, not a permanent declaration of ineligibility.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 8 → Part II: Management of the Waiting List — inactive status paragraph
primary_anchor.quote_hint: placed on the list in an inactive status, typically because their evaluation is incomplete
